name: ztest_fault_inject
prose: ztest test function (ztest.c:6419-6718; the packet name ztest_vdev_fault_inject does not exist, the slice cut the head); zd and id are unused and it returns void. It allocates two path buffers, takes ztest_vdev_lock itself and jumps to out (unlock, optional scrub, free buffers) if device removal is active, a raidz expansion is in progress (spa_raidz_expand set), the pool has not yet been scrubbed, maxfaults is 0 after the offline/online step, open of the chosen leaf file fails, or the mirror count changed during the loop (that case closes fd first). With ztest_name_lock (read) and SCL_STATE held it picks, with probability 1/2, a data/slog leaf from the top-level vdevs: if that vdev was found and maxfaults != 1 and it needs no resilver (or its resilver txg is non-zero) it randomly either closes the vdev's file descriptor (sets f_fd = -1), sets vdev_cant_read, or sets vdev_cant_write; these unreadable/unwritable/fd-close actions happen only in this data/slog branch. Otherwise it picks a cache (l2cache) device, returning via out if there are none (after releasing both locks), uses that device's path and sets maxfaults = INT_MAX; cache devices are never marked unreadable/unwritable here, they only take the later offline/online and bad-word injection. After the locks are released, if (maxfaults >= 2 or the vdev is a log) and a guid was chosen, then with 60 percent chance it offlines that vdev (temporary at random; VERIFY it is not EBUSY; for a log vdev under the write lock of ztest_name_lock) and otherwise brings it online. It then opens the leaf path and up to 999 times writes the 8-byte pattern at a random offset (skipping label areas for even/odd leaves), calling fatal() if pwrite fails, then closes fd. At out it unlocks, and if something was injected and zo_raid_do_expand is set it starts a scrub and waits while it runs; finally it frees both buffers.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 17 right (unreadable/unwritable/fd-close only for the data/slog branch, 6528-6553).

name: ztest_spa_import_export
prose: Static void (ztest.c:7443-7525) that exercises export and re-import of a pool under a new name. It first destroys any pool called newname (spa_destroy, result ignored), so newname does not need to be free beforehand. It opens oldname (VERIFY0), at random starts a scrub (result ignored), records the pool guid and closes it, exports the pool (VERIFY0, capturing its config), checks that spa_tryimport(config) returns a config (ASSERT, then frees it), and imports the config as newname: a non-zero error dumps the config and calls fatal(B_FALSE, ...), which is the only path that uses fatal. It then VERIFYs that importing again as newname and importing as oldname each return EEXIST, that spa_open(oldname) returns ENOENT, and that spa_open(newname) succeeds with the same guid (ASSERT3U), then closes the pool and frees the config. All VERIFY/ASSERT conditions panic (abort the process via the assertion handler), they do not call fatal(); the function has no return value and does not free the config on the fatal path.
note: Reviewers: original right (newname is destroyed first, 7458); round 15 right (VERIFY/ASSERT failures are assertion panics, only the spa_import error uses fatal(), 7494-7498).

name: pam_sm_chauthtok
prose: PAM password-change hook (pam_zfs_key.c:902-993, returns a PAM status). It returns PAM_PERM_DENIED if the effective uid is not 0, PAM_SERVICE_ERR if the config cannot be loaded or the user's uid is outside [uid_min, uid_max] (config freed in the second case). It then fetches the old token and, in an inner block, calls pam_zfs_init (PAM_SERVICE_ERR on failure, config freed), gets the dataset name (PAM_SERVICE_ERR if NULL), requires a non-null old token (PAM_SERVICE_ERR, frees the dataset), and decrypt_mount(old token, B_TRUE): on -1 it logs 'old token mismatch', frees dataset, ZFS handle (pam_zfs_free) and config and returns PAM_PERM_DENIED. If that check succeeds, the dataset string and the ZFS state from this first block are still held afterwards. Without PAM_UPDATE_AUTHTOK (the other branch) it only calls zfs_key_config_free and returns PAM_SUCCESS, so on that path the first-block dataset string is not freed and pam_zfs_free is not called (the first-block dataset is leaked and the ZFS handle stays initialised). With PAM_UPDATE_AUTHTOK: a missing new token, a NULL dataset (second lookup) or a failed decrypt_mount of the old key (when the key was not already loaded) each call pam_zfs_free and zfs_key_config_free, clear the stored passwords and return PAM_SERVICE_ERR; otherwise it calls change_key with the new token, unmounts/unloads again if it had to load the key, frees the second dataset string, calls pam_zfs_free and frees the config, clears both stored passwords and returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR if either clear or change_key failed, else PAM_SUCCESS. On update paths the first-block dataset string is also not freed.
note: Reviewers: original right (dataset leaked on the non-update path and the first-block dataset on update paths); round 15 right that pam_zfs_free is called on the update paths (pam_zfs_key.c:955, 962, 972, 983) while the non-update path skips it (989-991). Callees not read.

name: nv_alloc_sys
prose: Static allocator callback (nvpair_alloc_system.c:35-38) that returns kmem_alloc(size, (int)(uintptr_t)nva->nva_arg). It dereferences nva (so nva must be non-NULL) and uses its nva_arg as the kmem flags: the two statics defined in this file pass KM_SLEEP (nv_alloc_sleep) and KM_NOSLEEP (nv_alloc_nosleep). It adds no checks of its own: whatever kmem_alloc returns (a pointer, or NULL if the underlying allocator fails, which is only a possible outcome for KM_NOSLEEP in typical implementations) is returned unchanged, and for size 0 the result is whatever kmem_alloc gives for that size (not examined here). It has no other side effect and takes no locks of its own.
note: Reviewers: round 1 and round 2 reviewers contradict each other about kmem_alloc(0); the behaviour for size 0 and KM_SLEEP belongs to kmem_alloc, which I did not read, so the prose makes no claim about it. The old formal contract (unbound identifier null) is dropped.

name: nfs_enable_share_impl
prose: Writes the exports lines for one share to tmpfile (nfs.c:119-161, static, returns an int SA_* code). The share options are used as 'sa_shareopts', with the literal 'on' replaced by an empty string. It escapes the mountpoint with nfs_escape_mountpoint and returns that call's non-SA_OK code at once (nothing allocated yet). It then strdup's the options; if that fails it returns SA_SYSTEM_ERR directly, without freeing the escaped mountpoint, so that string leaks when need_free is set. Otherwise it splits the copy on ';': for each option set it sets fnd_semi once any ';' has been seen (s != NULL) and, while fnd_semi is true, skips (continue) a set consisting only of tabs/spaces; so an empty or whitespace-only set is skipped only when it is followed by a ';' or comes after one, while a single set with no ';' (including the empty string from 'on') is still written. For each set that is kept it writes the mountpoint, a tab, the translated options (translate_opts) and a newline; if any of those four writes fails, including translate_opts failing because its malloc returned NULL (it returns EOF), it prints 'failed to write to temporary file', sets rc = SA_SYSTEM_ERR and breaks out of the loop. It then frees the duplicated options, frees mp only if need_free, and returns rc (SA_OK or SA_SYSTEM_ERR).
note: Reviewers: original right (a line is written for an empty/whitespace-only first set when no ';' has been seen); round 2 right (first whitespace-only set is skipped when followed by ';', and the strdup failure leaks mp, nfs.c:133-135); round 15 right (translate_opts malloc failure returns EOF, nfs.c:93-94, giving the diagnostic and SA_SYSTEM_ERR).

name: changelist_gather
prose: Builds a prop_changelist_t for dataset zhp and property prop (libzfs_changelist.c:654-814; the slice is only the tail and the packet name changelist_add does not exist). Steps: zfs_alloc the list; for prop NAME, ZONED, MOUNTPOINT, SHARENFS or SHARESMB it reads the mountpoint property and sets legacy if it is 'legacy' or 'none'; it creates the AVL pool (compare by name when legacy, else by mountpoint) and tree, returning NULL after reporting EZFS_NOMEM and changelist_free if either creation fails. It maps prop to cl_prop: NAME gives MOUNTPOINT with cl_alldependents, ZONED gives MOUNTPOINT with cl_allchildren, CANMOUNT and VOLSIZE give MOUNTPOINT, other props are used as is, and stores cl_realprop. If cl_prop is not MOUNTPOINT, SHARENFS or SHARESMB it returns the (empty) list immediately, without adding zhp. Otherwise it sets cl_shareprop to the other share property for the share cases and gathers dependent datasets: with MOUNTPOINT and CL_GATHER_ITER_MOUNTED via zfs_iter_mounted(changelist_add_mounted), else with cl_alldependents via zfs_iter_dependents_v2, else for non-MOUNTPOINT props zfs_iter_filesystems_v2, else zfs_iter_children_v2 with change_one; any non-zero iteration result frees the list and returns NULL. It then re-opens zhp by name (zfs_open; NULL result frees the list and returns NULL), allocates a node with the new handle, cn_mounted (CL_GATHER_MOUNT_ALWAYS or zfs_is_mounted), cn_shared (zfs_is_shared), cn_zoned and cn_needpost = B_TRUE, and inserts it into the tree unless a node with the same key exists, in which case it frees the node and closes the extra handle. Finally, if cl_prop is MOUNTPOINT and the mountpoint was legacy/none, it sets cl_waslegacy unless canmount is noauto, and returns clp.
note: Slice cut the head. Callees not read.

name: make_dataset_handle_common
prose: Static int (libzfs_dataset.c:440-476). It first calls put_stats_zhdl(zhp, zc) and returns -1 if that returns non-zero. It then sets zfs_head_type from the dataset type: DMU_OST_ZVOL gives VOLUME and DMU_OST_ZFS gives FILESYSTEM; DMU_OST_OTHER sets errno = EINVAL and returns -1; only for any other type value, if dds_inconsistent is set, it sets errno = EBUSY and returns -1 (so an inconsistent ZVOL or ZFS dataset does not return EBUSY here), and otherwise (any remaining type) it calls abort(). It then sets zfs_type to SNAPSHOT if dds_is_snapshot, else VOLUME or FILESYSTEM by dds_type (abort() for anything else), and sets zhp->zpool_hdl = zpool_handle(zhp), returning -1 if that is NULL. Returns 0 on success. It has no locks and does not free zhp on failure (that is left to the caller).
note: Reviewers: original right (the -1 returns from put_stats_zhdl and zpool_handle); round 15 right (EBUSY is tested only in the branch after the ZVOL/ZFS/OTHER tests, libzfs_dataset.c:449-458). Callees not read.

name: zfs_show_diffs
prose: Runs 'zfs diff' (libzfs_diff.c:747-830; the slice is only the tail, the head is cut). It calls setup_differ_info; on failure it tears down the differ info and returns -1. It creates a pipe (pipe2 with O_CLOEXEC): failure sets an aux message, tears down and returns zfs_error(EZFS_PIPEFAILED). It sets the display flags and the two fds, starts the differ thread: if pthread_create fails it closes both pipe ends, tears down and returns zfs_error(EZFS_THREADCREATEFAILED). It then issues the ZFS_IOC_DIFF ioctl with the write end of the pipe. If the ioctl fails it sets an aux message by errno (EPERM and EXDEV special texts; other errors except EPIPE-with-differ-error), closes the write end, cancels and joins the thread, tears down and returns zfs_error(EZFS_DIFF, di.errbuf) when the differ recorded an error other than EPIPE, else zfs_error(EZFS_DIFFDATA, errbuf); read end pipefd[0] is not closed in this function on that path (it may be closed by the differ thread, not read). If the ioctl succeeds it closes the write end, joins the thread, and if di.zerr is non-zero returns zfs_error(EZFS_DIFF, di.errbuf) WITHOUT calling teardown_differ_info (the final di.zerr path at 824-827); otherwise it tears down the differ info and returns 0. The zfs_error values are -1 style return codes of that function (not read).
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 right: the final di.zerr != 0 return skips cleanup and does not close pipefd[0] in this function (libzfs_diff.c:824-827); not every failure path closes both pipe ends. Callees not read.

name: zpool_initialize_impl
prose: Static int (libzfs_pool.c:2478-2558) that starts, cancels or suspends initialisation on vdevs. It translates the vdev names to guids with zpool_translate_vdev_guids; if that fails (err non-zero) it goes to list_errors. Otherwise it calls lzc_initialize; on failure, if the returned errlist has an ZPOOL_INITIALIZE_VDEVS member it goes to list_errors with that per-vdev list; otherwise it sets an aux message for EINVAL with POOL_INITIALIZE_UNINIT, reports zpool_standard_error('operation failed') and goes to out (so per-vdev error translation is not used for these failures). If the call succeeded and wait is set, it calls lzc_wait_tag for each vdev guid and on the first failure reports zpool_standard_error_fmt and goes to out. list_errors prints, for each entry of the per-vdev error list, 'cannot initialize <path>' via zfs_error_fmt using xlate_init_err on the stored error (the path comes from guids_to_paths or the guid string). out frees vdev_guids, guids_to_paths and, if set, vd_errlist (the errlist returned by lzc_initialize is not freed here). The return value is 0 if err is 0 and -1 otherwise; the raw errno-like err is never returned.
note: Reviewers: original right (non-zero wait/lzc errors do not go through xlate_init_err unless a per-vdev list exists); round 15 WRONG: the function returns -1 on failure, not err (libzfs_pool.c:2557). Callees not read.

name: dump_snapshot
prose: Static iterator callback (libzfs_sendrecv.c:1150-1293) that sends one snapshot of the iterated dataset; it takes ownership of zhp and, on most paths, closes it. thissnap is the part after '@'. If the 'from' snapshot has not been seen and this is it: it gathers holds, sets seenfrom, copies the name into prevsnap, records prevsnap_obj, closes zhp and returns 0 without sending anything (so sdd is changed but this snapshot is not sent). If seento is already set or seenfrom is not yet set, it closes zhp and returns 0. Otherwise it notes whether this is the 'to' snapshot (sets seento), builds the lzc flags from sdd, and for a snapshot that is neither from nor to and not doall, excludes it (exclude = TRUE when not replicating, or when replicating and the snapshot is not a clone origin found through fsavl); if excluded or filter_cb returns false it closes zhp and returns 0. Otherwise it gathers holds, and when verbosity is non-zero estimates the size and prints it (adding to sdd->size). Unless dryrun, it fills the progress args and starts send_progress_thread: if pthread_create fails it closes zhp and returns that error; else it runs dump_ioctl and then send_progress_thread_exit; if that exit call fails it returns -1 immediately without closing zhp and without updating prevsnap. On the normal path it copies thissnap into prevsnap, stores prevsnap_obj, closes zhp and returns err (the dump_ioctl result, or 0 for a dry run).
note: Reviewers: original right (the from-snapshot branch returns 0 after updating seenfrom/prevsnap/prevsnap_obj); round 15 right that pthread_create failure closes zhp (1276), but note the -1 return after send_progress_thread_exit does not close it here (1285-1286).

name: recv_incremental_replication
prose: Static int (libzfs_sendrecv.c:3521-3819) that makes the local filesystem hierarchy under tofs match the stream's names and origins before an incremental replication receive. If flags->dryrun is set it returns 0 immediately, before reading anything or changing anything locally (so in a dry run the local hierarchy is not adjusted). Otherwise it reads fromsnap and the recursive flag from stream_nv and enters the 'again' pass: it allocates the deleted-guid list and gathers the local nvlist/avl with gather_nvlist, returning that call's non-zero error value directly if it fails. For each local filesystem it finds the matching stream entry; when the origin guids differ it may call recv_promote (progress = TRUE on success) and sets needagain, or, if created_before returns -1, it frees the local lists and returns -1; with flags->force it destroys local snapshots/filesystems missing from the stream via recv_destroy (failure sets needagain, success sets progress and records the guid in deleted); it renames filesystems with recv_rename when the parent or name differ (failure sets needagain, success sets progress), and may skip entries when parents are not yet in place (goto doagain / needagain). After the pass it frees the lists; if needagain and progress were both set it repeats from 'again'. Final return is the boolean (needagain || error != 0), so 0 or 1: individual destroy, rename and promote failures are not returned as their errno values (error holds only the last callee result and is only compared with 0). Hence the function returns 0, 1, -1 (created_before failure) or a gather_nvlist error value.
note: Reviewers: original right (dryrun returns 0 without adjusting names/origins, 3535-3536); round 15 right (rename/destroy failures set needagain, and the function ends in return (needagain || error != 0), 3818). Partly read: lines 3720-3790 (parent and rename handling) only checked for control flow.

name: zfs_setproctitle_init
prose: Void function (zutil_setproctitle.c:159-218) that prepares the process-title area. It returns without changing anything if argc < 0 or argv[0] is NULL. It sets nul to the end of argv[0] and end to the byte after it, then extends end across following argv strings that are contiguous in memory (the loop reads argv[i] for i >= argc until a NULL entry, so argv must be NULL-terminated, i.e. have argc+1 valid pointers) and then across contiguous envp strings, counting envp entries (envp must be NULL-terminated). It then duplicates argv[0] into SPT.arg0 (on strdup failure sets SPT.error = errno and returns), duplicates the program name and calls setprogname with it (same error handling), calls spt_copyenv(envc, envp) and spt_copyargs(argc, argv); a non-zero result from either is stored in SPT.error and the function returns. Only if everything succeeded does it set SPT.nul, SPT.base and SPT.end. It never sets SPT.error to 0 on success (it leaves the earlier value) and it does not itself rebuild environ; any environ change is inside spt_copyenv (not read). Resources already duplicated before a failure (arg0, progname) are not freed.
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (success does not write SPT.error = 0); round 15 right (the code reads argv[argc] and later entries until NULL, 175-176). spt_copyenv/spt_copyargs not read.

name: sha2_mac_final
prose: Finishes an HMAC-SHA2 operation (sha2_mod.c:458-537, static). It asserts ctx->cc_provider_private != NULL, then selects the digest length from hc_mech_type: only SHA512_HMAC_MECH_INFO_TYPE is accepted (digest_len = SHA512_DIGEST_LENGTH); any other mechanism returns CRYPTO_ARGUMENTS_BAD at once. If mac->cd_length is 0 or less than digest_len it sets mac->cd_length = digest_len and returns CRYPTO_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL. Both of these early returns leave the provider context allocated and unchanged (it is not freed or zeroed). Otherwise it finishes the inner hash (SHA2Final into a local digest), feeds it to the outer context, and by mac->cd_format: CRYPTO_DATA_RAW writes the outer digest into the raw buffer at cd_offset (directly, or via a local copy if digest_len differs from sha_digest_len); CRYPTO_DATA_UIO calls sha2_digest_final_uio and takes its result; any other format sets ret = CRYPTO_ARGUMENTS_BAD. After that it sets mac->cd_length = digest_len when ret is CRYPTO_SUCCESS and 0 otherwise, zeroes and kmem_frees the hmac context (sha2_hmac_ctx_t), sets ctx->cc_provider_private = NULL and returns ret, so these cleanup steps run on both the success and the failure outcome of the format switch.
note: Reviewers: original right (unsupported cd_format returns CRYPTO_ARGUMENTS_BAD, 523-524); round 15 WRONG: the code does set cd_length to 0 on failure and zeroes/frees cc_provider_private (sha2_mod.c:527-534). Callees (SHA2Final, sha2_digest_final_uio) not read.

name: lua_next
prose: Lua API function (lapi.c:1113-1127) that advances a table traversal. It takes the state lock, resolves idx to a stack slot (index2addr) and api_check-s that it is a table (a check that is active only when API checking is compiled in). It calls luaH_next(L, table, L->top - 1), which uses the key on the top of the stack as the current position and, when there is a next entry, replaces that key slot with the next key and writes the value above it; if that call returns non-zero the function does api_incr_top(L) so the stack ends up one slot larger than before the call (the popped key is replaced by key and value). If luaH_next returns 0 (no more elements) it removes the key with L->top -= 1, so the stack is one slot smaller. It then releases the lock and returns the luaH_next result (zero or non-zero; the code returns it as is). The behaviour of luaH_next for an invalid key (it may raise a Lua error) was not read.
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (net growth is one slot: key replaced and value pushed, not two); other reviewer rounds were truncated in the packet and are consistent with the code read. luaH_next not read.

name: nvlist_snprintf
prose: Formats an nvlist as text into buf of size bytes (nvpair.c:3753-3943) and returns the length that the full output would have (the sum of the snprintf return values, like snprintf, excluding any terminator), or a negative snprintf result immediately. If list is NULL it returns 0 without writing anything to buf. Otherwise, for each nvpair it calls snprintf into the remaining space (the NVP/NVPA macros and the explicit cases for boolean, boolean value, nvlist, nvlist array and the default 'bad config type' message), adds each rc to len, and after each write reduces size by rc (not below 0) and moves buf forward, or sets buf to NULL once size reaches 0, so later writes only count characters. Nested nvlists and nvlist-array members are formatted by recursive calls with the remaining buffer. A negative rc from any snprintf or recursive call is returned at once, abandoning the rest. With size 0 on entry nothing is written (no NUL is stored), and with a non-zero size each snprintf terminates its own piece, but a truncated output ends at buf_end with whatever snprintf stored (the function itself never stores a final NUL beyond that). The return value can exceed size - 1 when the output was truncated.
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (no terminator written when size is 0); round 2 right (list == NULL returns 0 without writing); the other truncated reviewer reasons are consistent with the code. Macro bodies NVP and NVPA not read (assumed to follow the same rc/size/buf pattern as the explicit cases; checked on the boolean, boolean-value, nvlist and default cases only).

name: zfs_readdir
prose: Reads directory entries into the caller's uio (zfs_vnops_os.c:1682-1931; the slice cut the head). It enters the filesystem with zfs_enter_verify_zp and returns that error if it fails; it looks up the parent object with sa_lookup (on failure it calls zfs_exit and returns the error). If eofp is NULL it uses a local variable instead (so eofp may be NULL). It returns EINVAL if the first iov length is 0, and returns 0 with *eofp = TRUE if the directory is unlinked (z_unlinked), both after zfs_exit. It allocates the zap attribute and a cursor (fresh for offsets <= 3, serialized otherwise) and chooses the output buffer: the iov itself for a single kernel-space iov, otherwise a kmem_alloc'd temporary; if ncookies is non-NULL it also malloc's a cookie array. The loop emits '.', '..', optionally the .zfs control directory entry, then ZAP entries until bytes_wanted is reached: a ZAP retrieve error sets *eofp for ENOENT and ends the loop, or any other error jumps to update; an entry with unexpected integer size/count sets ENXIO; if an entry does not fit and nothing has been output yet it sets EINVAL, else the loop stops. After the loop it clears the prefetch flag, trims *ncookies, and for the single kernel-space iov advances the iov and resid directly, else copies with zfs_uiomove (an error there is kept and the offset is re-read from the uio). At update it finishes the cursor, frees the attribute and temporary buffer, converts ENOENT to 0, updates the access time, stores the offset in the uio, calls zfs_exit, frees the cookie array and zeroes *ncookies/*cookies when error != 0 and cookies was given, and returns error.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 WRONG: eofp is replaced by &local_eof when NULL (zfs_vnops_os.c:1718-1719), so it may be NULL. Callees not read.

name: zfs_setattr
prose: Applies vattr changes to a znode (zfs_vnops_os.c:2291-2981; the slice is the tail, the head is cut). Before the zfs_enter_verify_zp it returns 0 if the mask is empty and EINVAL if AT_NOSET is set; after entering it returns (with zfs_exit) EINVAL for FUID-incompatible requests or AT_SIZE on non-regular/non-FIFO files, EISDIR for AT_SIZE on a directory, EPERM for immutable files, EOVERFLOW for out-of-range times, EOPNOTSUPP for project-id requests when unsupported, EINVAL for an invalid project id, EROFS on a read-only filesystem, any error from zfs_freesp (AT_SIZE is applied first), policy/permission errors (zfs_zaccess, policy checks), and EPERM for AT_XVATTR/XAT_REPARSE. Then, for uid/gid/project changes it looks up and locks the xattr directory znode (attrzp), and returns EDQUOT (via out2, before any transaction) if a quota check fails; for AT_MODE it builds the ACL, EPERM in restricted mode (via out). It then creates the dmu transaction and assigns it (DMU_TX_WAIT); an assign error goes to out. After assignment it updates the in-memory fields and the bulk attribute arrays under z_acl_lock: uid/gid, mode/ACL, times, size, project id (the project id is set both on zp->z_projid and, when attrzp exists, on attrzp->z_projid, 2821-2826 and 2895-2899), and the xvattr flags. At the out label: on err == 0 with attrzp it applies the xattr bulk update; it frees the ACL and fuid info; on err it aborts the transaction (and vput's attrzp), but on success it applies the bulk update to zp, commits the transaction, and for attrzp may call zfs_setattr_dir (its error becomes the function's error AFTER the commit) and vput's attrzp. Finally (out2) if err == 0 and the objset sync is ALWAYS it sets err = zil_commit(zilog, 0), calls zfs_exit and returns err. So a zfs_setattr_dir or zil_commit failure is reported after the transaction was already committed.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 right (zfs_setattr_dir/zil_commit failures occur after commit, 2985-2995); round 17 WRONG (the project id is also stored in attrzp->z_projid, 2822-2823). Partly read: lines 2455-2680 (policy and xvattr permission logic) were only skimmed for return paths; the many XVA_ISSET_REQ branches were not read line by line.

name: zfs_do_rename_impl
prose: Static int (zfs_vnops_os.c:3316-3548) that performs the rename; it enters the filesystem itself (zfs_enter_verify_zp on tdzp, zfs_verify_zp on sdzp, szp and tzp), so the caller must not have entered it already; a verify failure after the enter calls zfs_exit and returns that error. Failures that jump to out (so zfs_exit still runs, after the optional ZFS_SYNC_ALWAYS commit): EILSEQ for an invalid UTF-8 target name; success (error = 0, nothing done) if source and target vnode are the same; EXDEV if either is a directory with a mount on it; EINVAL if source and target dirs differ in XATTR-ness; EXDEV on project-id inheritance mismatch; the error of zfs_zaccess_rename; for a directory source EINVAL when renaming '.', sdzp == szp or an ISDOTDOT component, or the error of zfs_rename_check; for an existing target EEXIST if AT_RENAME_NOREPLACE, ENOTDIR (dir onto non-dir) or EISDIR (non-dir onto dir). It then begins vn_seqc writes, fires the vnevents, builds and assigns a transaction (a dmu_tx_assign failure aborts the tx and goes to out_seq). With the tx assigned it destroys an existing target link, creates the new link (ZRENAMING), updates the source flags, destroys the old link and logs the rename; if the old-link destroy fails it removes the just-created new link (VERIFY0) and keeps that error; on success with the namecache it updates it. It always commits the transaction after assignment (dmu_tx_commit at 3532, also when error is non-zero), then ends the seqc writes. At out, if error == 0 and the objset sync property is ALWAYS it assigns error = zil_commit(zilog, 0) (the source assigns that result; the reviewer's claim that zil_commit returns void conflicts with this line), then zfs_exit and returns error.
note: Reviewers: original right (the function enters the filesystem itself, 3332-3337); round 15 contradicts line 3543-3544 where the zil_commit result is stored in error, I did not read zil_commit's declaration. Callees not read.

name: zfs_symlink
prose: Creates a symbolic link (zfs_vnops_os.c:3613-3743; the slice cut the head). It returns ENAMETOOLONG for a too-long name before entering the filesystem, then enters with zfs_enter_verify_zp (returns its error). After the enter every early failure calls zfs_exit and returns: EILSEQ for an invalid UTF-8 name, ENAMETOOLONG if the link target length exceeds MAXPATHLEN, the error of zfs_acl_ids_create, of zfs_dirent_lookup(ZNEW) (name already exists), or of zfs_zaccess(ACE_ADD_FILE), and EDQUOT on overquota; the acl ids are freed on those after they were created. Then getnewvnode_reserve() is called and a transaction is built and assigned; if dmu_tx_assign fails it frees the acl ids, aborts the tx, drops the getnewvnode reserve, exits and returns the error. (So the getnewvnode reserve is dropped only on that path and on the final path, not on the early returns before it was taken, which never took it.) With the tx assigned it makes the znode (zfs_mknode), writes the link text (sa_update when the znode is SA, else zfs_sa_symlink; the sa_update result is overwritten by the later error value), sets the size, and calls zfs_link_create; if that fails it deletes the new znode, unlocks and releases it; otherwise it logs the symlink. It then frees the acl ids, commits the transaction (also on a zfs_link_create failure), drops the getnewvnode reserve, and on success stores the new znode in *zpp (so *zpp is written only on success) and, if the objset sync is ALWAYS, sets error = zil_commit(zilog, 0). It calls zfs_exit and returns error (0 or the zfs_link_create/zil_commit/earlier error).
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 right (the transaction commit/abort and getnewvnode reserve drop do not happen on the early-return paths, which precede them, zfs_vnops_os.c:3629-3672).

name: zfs_lookup
prose: Directory lookup (zfs_vnops_os.c:751-1004; the slice cut the head). Without LOOKUP_XATTR it returns ENOTDIR if dvp is not a directory and EIO if the dnode's SA handle is NULL; these two returns, and a failing zfs_enter_verify_zp, happen before *vpp is assigned, so *vpp is left untouched there (it is not set to NULL on them). After the enter it sets *vpp = NULL. With LOOKUP_XATTR it returns EOPNOTSUPP if xattrs are unsupported, EINVAL if the directory is itself an xattr dir, or the zfs_get_xattrdir error; otherwise it sets *vpp to the xattr dir vnode, checks execute permission on it and on a zaccess failure vrele's it and returns the error (while *vpp still holds that pointer). Otherwise, unless cached, it checks execute permission (error returned, zfs_exit called) and returns EILSEQ for an invalid UTF-8 name. For '..' at the root of a snapshot-mounted zfsvfs it goes through the control-directory root and the 'snapshot' entry and returns that result. For the '.zfs' name in a dataset with a ctldir it returns ENOENT if the snapdir is disabled, ENOTSUP if it is the last component of a non-lookup operation, else the control root. Otherwise it loops: zfs_dirlook, zfs_exit, lock the found vnode (zfs_lookup_lock; on failure *vpp = NULL and return); for non-dotdot it stops; for dotdot it re-enters, reads the parent and repeats until the found vnode is not the directory's parent or an error occurs. On any error *vpp is set to NULL. For the last component of CREATE/RENAME, ENOENT becomes EJUSTRETURN; the dotdot seqc check may clear MAKEENTRY; it adds a negative cache entry for ENOENT and a positive entry on success, when the namecache is enabled and not replaying; it returns error.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 right (*vpp not NULLed on the early ENOTDIR/EIO and enter-failure returns, 771-782). Callees not read.

name: define_ddi_strtox(type, valtype)
prose: Macro (spl-generic.c:212-280) that generates ddi_strtol, ddi_strtoull and ddi_strtoll (invoked with (l, long), (ull, unsigned long long) and (ll, long long)); the generated function is int ddi_strto<type>(const char *str, char **endptr, int base, valtype *result). Behaviour of the generated function: it skips leading characters found in the set ' \t\n\r\f' with strchr(set, *ptr); because strchr also matches the terminating NUL of the searched set when *ptr is '\0', the skip loop does not stop at the end of str, so an empty or all-whitespace string is walked past its terminator (an out-of-bounds read) until some non-whitespace byte is found; the subsequent 'strlen(ptr) == 0 returns EINVAL' test therefore only triggers if the loop ended on a NUL. It then accepts one '-' (sets minus) or '+'. If base is 0 it detects the base from str[0] (the original string start, not the post-sign pointer): '0x' followed by a hex digit gives base 16 (ptr += 2), '0' followed by 0-7 gives base 8 (ptr += 1), a leading '0' with anything else returns EINVAL, otherwise base 10. It then accumulates digits (decimal digits and letters, stopping at the first character whose digit value is >= base or at a non-alphanumeric); it returns ERANGE if the accumulated value decreases ('last_value > value', a wrap-around test), which is only a reliable overflow test for the unsigned variant. At least one digit is not required: with no digits it stores 0 and returns 0. It stores minus ? -value : value in *result, sets *endptr (if non-NULL) to the first unparsed character, and returns 0. On the EINVAL and ERANGE returns *result and *endptr are not written.
note: Macro-generated; the name is the definition head. The old round did not note the strchr-NUL over-read; checked against the macro text only (not compiled). Callers not read.

name: zone_dataset_attach
prose: Attaches a dataset name to the zone (user namespace) given by userns_fd (spl-zone.c:183-231). Without CONFIG_USER_NS it returns ENXIO immediately. With it: it returns the error of zone_dataset_cred_check (credential check), of zone_dataset_name_check (name check, also yields dsnamelen) or of user_ns_get (resolves the fd to a user namespace), in that order and before taking the lock. It then takes zone_datasets_lock and holds it until the end: it looks up the zone's dataset list by user_ns_zoneid; if none exists it kmem_allocs a new zone_datasets_t, initialises its lists, stores the userns, takes a reference with get_user_ns and adds it to the global zone_datasets list; if one exists and already contains the dataset name it releases the lock and returns EEXIST (nothing else is added; whether the reference from user_ns_get is released on this path is not handled in this function). Otherwise it kmem_allocs a zone_dataset_t sized for the name, copies the name with strlcpy and appends it to the zone's dataset list, releases the lock and returns 0. The lock is therefore held across the allocations, the strlcpy and get_user_ns as well as the list lookup and update.
note: Reviewers: original right (ENXIO without CONFIG_USER_NS); round 15 right (the lock covers kmem_alloc, strlcpy and get_user_ns, spl-zone.c:199-226). Callees not read.

name: zfs_zaccess_common
prose: Common access check (zfs_acl.c:2483-2537). It first sets *working_mode = v4_mode and *check_privs = B_TRUE. If v4_mode is 0 or the filesystem is replaying (z_replay) it sets *working_mode = 0 and returns 0. If zfs_zaccess_dataset_check(zp, v4_mode) returns non-zero it sets *check_privs = B_FALSE and returns that error with *working_mode still equal to v4_mode. If skipaclchk is set it sets *working_mode = 0 and returns 0. If v4_mode contains data-write bits, zp is not a directory and ZFS_READONLY is set in z_pflags it returns EPERM, leaving *working_mode equal to v4_mode and *check_privs TRUE. If ZFS_ACL_TRIVIAL is set it returns zfs_zaccess_trivial(zp, working_mode, cr, mnt_ns); otherwise it returns zfs_zaccess_aces_check(zp, working_mode, B_FALSE, cr, mnt_ns). Those last two return values are passed through unchanged and may be whatever those callees return (the reviewer reports -1 from the ACE check); in those two cases *working_mode is the callee's output.
note: Reviewers: original right (the ACE-check return is passed through, may be -1 rather than an errno, per its callee; not read); round 15 right (*working_mode stays v4_mode on the dataset-check failure and the READONLY EPERM paths, 2489, 2500-2502, 2527-2530).

name: zfsctl_snapdir_mkdir
prose: Creates a snapshot by mkdir in .zfs/snapshot (zfs_ctldir.c:1012-1047). It returns EACCES immediately if the zfs_admin_snapshot tunable is off (nothing allocated). Otherwise it kmem_allocs a dataset-name buffer and: returns EILSEQ (via out) if dirname fails zfs_component_namecheck; fills dsname from the objset; returns the error of zfs_secpolicy_snapshot_perms(dsname, cr) if non-zero; calls dmu_objset_snapshot_one(dsname, dirname) and returns its error if non-zero; otherwise it calls zfsctl_snapdir_lookup(dip, dirname, ipp, ...) and returns its result. So if the snapshot was created and the following lookup fails, the error is returned although the snapshot remains in existence. out frees the name buffer. The admin-snapshot setting and the dirname validity are not preconditions: they are checked here, giving EACCES and EILSEQ.
note: Reviewers: original right (snapshot remains if the lookup fails, 1036-1042); round 15 right (EACCES and EILSEQ are returned for disabled admin snapshots and bad names, 1019-1026). Callees not read.

name: zfs_remove
prose: Removes a non-directory name from directory dzp (zfs_vnops_os.c:992-1211; the slice cut the head). It returns EINVAL if name is NULL, enters with zfs_enter_verify_zp (returns its error), then zfs_dirent_lock the entry: on failure it frees realnmp, exits and returns the error. Past that, failures that go to out: the error of zfs_zaccess_delete, EPERM if the target is a directory. It then builds a transaction (holds on the dir, the znode, possibly its blocks, xattr dir and external ACL when the object may be deleted now); dmu_tx_assign failure unlocks the dirent lock and, for ERESTART, aborts the tx, releases zp and xzp and retries from top; for any other error it aborts, releases zp/xzp, exits and returns the error. After assign, zfs_link_destroy runs; if it fails it commits the tx and goes to out. On success, if the znode became unlinked it is added to the unlinked set (when it cannot be deleted immediately) or deleted now (delete_now, including the unlinked xattr dir); otherwise (the object still has other hard links, unlinked false) neither happens and the znode is simply released. The transaction is committed and at out the name buffer and the dirent lock are released, zp is released with zrele when delete_now else zfs_zrele_async, xzp is released async if present, and with ZFS_SYNC_ALWAYS and no error the result of zil_commit becomes the return value; zfs_exit then runs and error is returned.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 right (with remaining hard links the target znode is only released, not freed or put in the unlinked set, zfs_vnops_os.c:1177-1199). Partly read: 1054-1135 (delete_now/xattr logic) skimmed.

name: zfs_mkdir
prose: Creates a directory (zfs_vnops_os.c:1235-1407; the slice cut the head). It returns EINVAL if FUIDs are unavailable but needed, or dirname is NULL (before entering), then zfs_enter_verify_zp (error returned); after entering, each failure calls zfs_exit and returns: EINVAL if dzp is an xattr dir, EILSEQ for an invalid UTF-8 name, the error of secpolicy_xvattr or of zfs_acl_ids_create. At 'top' it takes the dirent lock (zfs_dirent_lock with the new-name flag): failure frees the acl ids, exits and returns its error. Then access check on ACE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY (error: frees acl ids, unlocks, exits, returns) and EDQUOT if over quota (same cleanup). It builds and assigns a transaction: on a dmu_tx_assign failure it unlocks the dirent lock and, for ERESTART, aborts the tx and retries from top; for other errors it frees the acl ids, aborts the tx, exits and returns the error. With the tx assigned it makes the znode (zfs_mknode) and zfs_link_create; if that fails it deletes the znode, removes the inode from the hash and goes to out; otherwise it syncs fuids and writes the create log record. At out it frees the acl ids, commits the transaction (also after a link failure), unlocks the dirent lock; on error it releases zp, else it returns the new znode through *zpp and applies zil_commit when the objset sync is ALWAYS (its result becomes the return value); then zfs_exit and return error.
note: Slice cut the head. Previously unreviewed by a second reviewer; checked against the code. The exact *zpp assignment line was not displayed in my filtered view (comment lines are stripped); it is in the else branch at about 1397-1400.

name: zfs_rmdir
prose: Removes a directory (zfs_vnops_os.c:1426-1537). It returns EINVAL if name is NULL (before entering the filesystem; zfs_exit is not called there), and enters with zfs_enter_verify_zp itself (so the caller must not have entered it already; failure returns its error without holding anything). It takes the dirent lock (zfs_dirent_lock): on failure it exits and returns the error, no zp to release. After that, failures go to out: the error of zfs_zaccess_delete, ENOTDIR if the target is not a directory, EINVAL if the target is cwd. It then takes the target's z_name_lock and z_parent_lock as writer, creates and assigns a transaction (on failure it releases both locks and the dirent lock; for ERESTART it aborts, releases zp and retries from top; otherwise it aborts, releases zp, exits and returns the error), calls zfs_link_destroy and, if that succeeded, writes the log record, commits the transaction and releases both rw locks. At out it unlocks the dirent lock, releases zp (zrele), applies zil_commit when the sync property is ALWAYS and error is 0 (the result becomes error), calls zfs_exit and returns error. EEXIST is not produced by this function's own checks.
note: Reviewers: original right (the function enters the filesystem itself; name == NULL returns before the enter; EEXIST is not an rmdir result); round 2 right (not every return exits: the NULL-name return does not call zfs_exit and early errors hold no locks).

name: zpl_xattr_set
prose: Sets or removes (value == NULL) an extended attribute (zpl_xattr.c:600-673, static). It holds a cred reference and marks fstrans, enters with zpl_enter_verify_zp (on failure it skips the lock and returns that error), and takes z_xattr_lock as writer. It finds where the attribute currently lives (__zpl_xattr_where, a bitmask of XATTR_IN_SA / XATTR_IN_DIR). If that call fails with an error other than -ENODATA it returns that error; for -ENODATA (attribute absent) it returns -ENODATA when XATTR_REPLACE is set, returns 0 (nothing to remove) when value is NULL, and otherwise continues with error 0; if the attribute exists it sets -EEXIST and returns it when XATTR_CREATE is set, otherwise continues. If the file system uses SA and the znode is SA-based and (xattr=sa is set, or this is a removal of an SA attribute) it tries zpl_xattr_set_sa; on success it removes any directory copy (zpl_xattr_set_dir with a NULL value, whose result is ignored) and returns 0; if the SA attempt fails it falls through. Otherwise it calls zpl_xattr_set_dir with the value; on success, if the attribute was previously in SA it clears the SA copy with zpl_xattr_set_sa(NULL) and ignores that result. At out it releases the lock, exits, drops fstrans and the cred, asserts error <= 0 and returns error (0 or a negative errno). So after a successful set exactly one location is written, but a failure to clear the other copy is not reported; after a successful removal the attribute is cleared in the location(s) the code tried and errors of clearing the second location are ignored.
note: Reviewers: original right (after a successful removal the attribute is in neither SA nor dir, not exactly one); round 15 right (errors from clearing the other location are ignored, zpl_xattr.c:652-653 and 662-663). Callees not read.

name: abd_raidz_gen_iterate
prose: Walks the parity abds and the data abd in lock step and calls func_raidz_gen on each mapped chunk (abd.c:1057-1133). It asserts parity <= 3; for each parity abd it checks off + csize <= abd_size and initialises an iterator at off; if dsize > 0 it asserts dabd is set, that off + dsize <= dabd->abd_size, and initialises the data iterator (c_dabd). It enters a critical section and loops while csize > 0 (the parity length controls the loop, not dsize): it maps each parity iterator, takes len = min(csize, the parity map sizes); if dsize > 0 it also maps the data iterator, takes len = min(len, data map size) and dlen = len (not clamped to the remaining dsize), otherwise it uses daddr = NULL and dlen = 0. It asserts len > 0 and that len is a multiple of 512, calls func_raidz_gen(caddrs, daddr, len, dlen), unmaps and advances the data iterator by dlen and subtracts dlen from dsize (only when dsize > 0), then unmaps and advances each parity iterator by len and subtracts len from csize. So dsize may be smaller than csize (later calls then get daddr NULL and dlen 0 once dsize reaches 0) and dsize may be larger than csize (the loop ends when csize is 0 and the rest of dsize is not consumed). It exits the critical section and returns void.
note: Reviewers: original right (loop is bounded by csize; dsize > csize leaves data unconsumed); round 2 right (dsize < csize gives later calls NULL/0, not dlen == len); round 15 right (dsize >= csize is not required). The advance/map helpers were not read.

name: arc_change_state
prose: Moves an ARC header between arc states and adjusts size accounting (arc.c:2430-2622, void). It asserts the hash lock is held and new_state != old_state. If the header has an L1 part it reads old_state, the reference count, and update_old (buf, pabd or raw data present); otherwise old_state is arc_l2c_only, refcnt 0 and update_old false. update_new starts equal to update_old, and both become TRUE when the old or new state is a ghost state respectively. If refcnt == 0: for a non-anon, non-l2c-only old state it removes the header from that state's multilist (and decrements evictable space) only if its list node is active, and for a non-anon, non-l2c-only new state it inserts it into the new state's multilist and increments evictable space. If new_state is arc_anon and the header is in the hash table it removes it with buf_hash_remove. Then, for update_new (and new state not l2c_only) it adds the header's sizes to new_state->arcs_size (logical size for ghost states, otherwise each non-shared buf, the pabd and the raw data), and for update_old (old state not l2c_only) removes the sizes from the old state in the same way. Finally, only if the header HAS an L1 part it sets hdr->b_l1hdr.b_state = new_state, and, if it also has an L2 header and new_state is not l2c_only, it decrements the l2 arcstats for the old state, sets b_l2hdr.b_arcs_state = new_state->arcs_state and increments the stats. A header with no L1 part does not get b_state or b_l2hdr.b_arcs_state written. Returns void.
note: Reviewers: original right (b_state is set only when HDR_HAS_L1HDR, 2613-2614); round 15 right (the L2 arcs_state update is nested inside the HDR_HAS_L1HDR test, 2616-2620).

name: l2arc_evict
prose: Evicts L2ARC buffers from the area about to be overwritten (arc.c:9125-9340, void). dev must be a valid pointer (it is dereferenced at entry to read l2ad_vdev, even when all is set); vd and l2ad_spa may be NULL only when all is TRUE (ASSERTs). At top it sets taddr to dev->l2ad_hand + distance, or to l2ad_end with rerun = TRUE when that sum would pass l2ad_end. If !all: when dev->l2ad_first is set it jumps to out without evicting anything (l2ad_evict is not advanced and l2ad_first is not cleared here); otherwise it optionally trims the freed range (dropping and retaking the SCL_L2ARC config lock around vdev_trim_simple) and raises l2ad_evict to at least taddr. Under l2ad_mtx it frees log-block pointer entries from the tail of l2ad_lbptr_list that are no longer valid (all of them when all is TRUE), then walks the buffer list from the tail: it try-locks each header's hash lock (on contention it drops l2ad_mtx, waits on that lock, and restarts at retry), stops the walk (break) when !all and the header's device address is outside [l2ad_hand, l2ad_evict), and otherwise evicts the header: an L2-only header is moved to arc_anon and destroyed; a header that has an L1 part is flagged L2_EVICTED if it is being read and its l2hdr is destroyed. It then unlocks l2ad_mtx. At out, if !all and rerun is set it resets l2ad_hand and l2ad_evict to l2ad_start, clears l2ad_first and repeats from top (so the wrap-around case evicts in two passes); then, if !all, it asserts hand + distance <= l2ad_end and hand <= l2ad_evict when not l2ad_first. Returns void.
note: Reviewers: original right (dev is dereferenced unconditionally even when all is set, 9132); round 15 right (the l2ad_first early exit does no eviction and does not advance l2ad_evict or clear l2ad_first in that pass, 9164-9170).

name: dbuf_dirty
prose: Marks a dbuf dirty in the transaction's txg and returns its dirty record (dbuf.c:2322-2578; the slice cut the head). The caller must hold a reference on db (ASSERT on db_holds) and the tx must have an assigned txg; the caller does NOT have to hold the dnode entered: dbuf_dirty itself calls DB_DNODE_ENTER(db) near the top and DB_DNODE_EXIT before returning. It takes db_mtx and, if the dbuf already has a dirty record for tx->tx_txg, releases the lock and returns that existing record with no change (2374-2379). Otherwise it creates a new dirty record (the lines between 2405 and 2478, including arc_release or data copy for level-0 non-bonus buffers, freed-range cleanup and dirtycnt update, were only skimmed), drops db_mtx, and for bonus and spill buffers it links the record to dn_dirty_records[txgoff] under dn_mtx, calls dnode_setdirty and returns the record. For other buffers it takes dn_struct_rwlock as reader if not already held for write, and, if the block is not the top level, finds or holds the parent dbuf (dbuf_hold_level), drops the rwlock if it took it, re-takes db_mtx, and links the record into the parent's dr_children only if the dbuf's first dirty record is still dr or the object is the meta dnode (this guards against dbuf_undirty having changed the list while db_mtx was dropped; if that test fails the record is not linked to the parent, 2553-2561), then releases the parent hold and db_mtx. For a top-level block (the dnode's own block pointers) it links the record directly into dn_dirty_records[txgoff] under dn_mtx and drops the rwlock if taken. It returns the record in all of these paths.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewers: original right (dbuf_dirty calls DB_DNODE_ENTER itself, 2332-2334); round 15 right (the parent link is conditional on the record still being first or the meta dnode, 2553-2554). Partly read: lines 2405-2478 (state handling, arc_release, free-range clearing) not read in detail.

name: receive_object
prose: Applies one DRR_OBJECT record on the receive side (dmu_recv.c:1913-2195). Before any transaction exists it returns EINVAL for an invalid or inconsistent record: a DMU_OT_NONE or invalid type/bonus type, oversized block size or bonus length, raw-stream field mismatches (object below or outside or_firstobj etc.), non-raw streams with raw fields or flags, and for a dmu_object_info result other than 0, ENOENT or EEXIST; it also returns the error of dmu_free_long_object (or of dmu_object_info in the slot loop) without a transaction. When the object exists (err == 0) it may free its old contents with dmu_free_long_object and return that error; for EEXIST it returns EINVAL if the object still exists; for ENOENT it records that a sync is needed. For objects needing several dnode slots it checks and frees the following slots (errors other than ENOENT/EEXIST are returned). It then creates a transaction and assigns it: a dmu_tx_assign failure aborts the tx and returns that error. With the tx assigned it claims a new object, reclaims an existing one with changed properties, or removes a stale spill block; if that fails it commits the transaction (not aborts) and returns EINVAL. With crypt params it sets them up (failure: commit the tx and return EINVAL); for raw streams it sets blocksize, nlevels and max blkid (VERIFY0); if a bonus buffer was sent it holds the dnode and bonus, copies the bonus data (byteswapping when needed) and releases them. It records the resume state, commits the transaction and returns 0. Errors after objects/ranges have been freed return without undoing that freeing, so partial state can remain.
note: Reviewers: original right (ranges and objects may already have been freed when an errno is returned); round 15 right (the early EINVAL and dmu_free_long_object paths return before any transaction exists, so there is nothing to abort or commit there). Partly read: lines 2091-2182 (crypto params and bonus copy) only skimmed.

name: receive_process_record
prose: Dispatches one receive record to its handler (dmu_recv.c:3142-3263; the slice is the middle of it). It asserts bytes_read does not go backwards and stores rrd->bytes_read in rwa->bytes_read. In heal mode, for any record that is not DRR_WRITE it frees rrd->abd (or else the payload) and returns 0 without processing. In normal mode, for any record that is not DRR_WRITE it first flushes the pending write batch (flush_write_batch); if that fails it frees the abd or payload and returns the error. Then by type: OBJECT calls receive_object and frees the payload; FREEOBJECTS, FREE, OBJECT_RANGE, REDACT call their handlers; WRITE calls receive_process_write_record and then frees rrd->abd when in heal mode, or when the result is not EAGAIN (an EAGAIN result leaves the abd to the batch); WRITE_EMBEDDED calls its handler and frees the payload; SPILL calls receive_spill, frees the abd if it failed, and clears both abd and payload pointers. The default case (unknown record type) sets err = EINVAL and does not free rrd->abd or rrd->payload. If err is non-zero it logs with dprintf_drr. It returns err, so the abd and payload are not freed on every non-EAGAIN path: the unknown-type EINVAL path leaves them to the caller, and some handlers' results are returned without any free of fields they did not take.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer original right (contract/EAGAIN/ownership not enumerated); round 15 right (the default EINVAL path frees nothing, dmu_recv.c:3255-3256). Callees not read.

name: dmu_recv_end_sync
prose: Sync-task callback that finishes a receive (dmu_recv.c:3671-3823, void). It logs 'finish receiving' in the pool history and clears os_raw_receive. Heal mode (drc_heal): it only frees drc_keynvl; no snapshot is created and DS_FLAG_INCONSISTENT is not cleared in this branch. Non-heal, existing filesystem (!drc_newfs): it holds the origin head, with drc_force destroys the snapshots newer than the received one, applies a raw key if drc_keynvl is set (then frees it), swaps the clone with the origin head, snapshots the origin head under drc_tosnap, sets that snapshot's creation time and guid from the stream header, clears DS_FLAG_INCONSISTENT on both the new snapshot and the head, records newsnapobj, releases the head and destroys the temporary receive dataset. Non-heal, new filesystem: it snapshots the dataset, sets the snapshot's creation time and guid, clears DS_FLAG_INCONSISTENT on the snapshot and the dataset, removes the saved resume state (ZAP fields) if present and records newsnapobj. After the branches, if not heal, raw and drc_ivset_guid != 0 it zapifies the new snapshot object and stores DS_FIELD_IVSET_GUID (so the IVSET GUID is not stored in the heal case); for a non-raw receive into an encrypted dataset it removes the keystore mapping; finally, for all three branches including heal, it disowns the dataset and sets drc->drc_ds = NULL.
note: Reviewers: original right (the heal path creates no snapshot and does not clear INCONSISTENT); round 15 right (the IVSET_GUID update is guarded by !drc_heal, 3801). Callees not read.

name: dmu_redact_snap
prose: Creates or resumes a redaction bookmark and runs the redaction (dmu_redact.c:1004-1204; the packet name dsl_redact does not exist, the slice cut the head). It returns the error of dsl_pool_hold directly if that fails. Then it allocates the bookmark-name buffer, holds snapname (error goes to out), long-holds it and returns EINVAL (via out) if it is not a snapshot or its objset cannot be opened, EALREADY if it already has the redacted-datasets feature active. For each name in redactnvl it holds the dataset and objset and requires it to be earlier than snapname (EINVAL otherwise) and not already redacted (EALREADY); the first error goes to out. It builds '<snapname>#<redactbook>'; if that does not fit, it releases the pool, frees the name buffer and args and returns ENAMETOOLONG directly, WITHOUT releasing the long-held and held target dataset or the redaction-snapshot holds (this is the only path that skips out's dataset release). If the bookmark already exists: EEXIST if it is not a redaction bookmark or if it was already fully completed (last blkid and object UINT64_MAX), EIO if its redaction list cannot be held, ESRCH if the snapshot list does not match (count or guids); then it resumes. Otherwise it releases the pool and creates the redaction bookmark with dsl_bookmark_create_redacted (error goes to out). It starts one traverse thread per redaction snapshot and a merge thread and calls perform_redaction(os, new_rl, rmta), keeping its result in err; then it destroys the queue and frees rmta. At out it frees the name buffer, releases the redaction list holds, each redaction snapshot's long hold and hold, the args array, the pool (if still held) and the target dataset's long hold and hold, and returns err.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 17 right (the ENAMETOOLONG return at dmu_redact.c:1082-1088 does not release the target dataset). Callees (perform_redaction, the threads) not read.

name: dump_dnode
prose: Emits a DRR_OBJECT record for one dnode (dmu_send.c:713-805, static). If object < dscp->dsc_resume_object it returns 0 immediately (ASSERTing the distance fits within one dnode block) and sends nothing. If dnp is NULL or its type is DMU_OT_NONE it returns the result of dump_freeobjects(dscp, object, 1). Otherwise, if an operation is pending it flushes it with dump_record(dscp, NULL, 0): failure returns EINTR, success clears the pending op. It then zeroes the record, fills the object fields from dnp (type, bonus type/len, block size clamped to SPA_OLD_MAXBLOCKSIZE unless the large-blocks feature is set, dn_slots, checksum, compress, toguid); for a raw send it asserts the bp is encrypted, may set DRR_RAW_BYTESWAP, copies maxblkid, indblkshift, nlevels and nblkptr, and, only when the rounded bonus length is non-zero, returns EINVAL if the bonus length exceeds DN_MAX_BONUS_LEN or else sets raw_bonuslen and uses it as the bonus length. It sets DRR_OBJECT_SPILL when the dnode has a spill block pointer. It then calls dump_record with the bonus buffer (failure returns EINTR) and dump_free for the object's whole data range (failure returns EINTR), and finally returns EINTR if dscp->dsc_err is non-zero, else 0.
note: Reviewers: original and round 2 right (EINTR from the pending-record flush and from the final dump_record, 736-737, 793-794); round 15 WRONG: the code does test dump_free's result and then dsc_err (797-802), and the raw bonus-length handling is inside 'if (bonuslen != 0)' (777). Callees not read.

name: dmu_tx_try_assign
prose: Static int (dmu_tx.c:1050-1151) that tries once to assign the tx to an open txg. It asserts tx_txg == 0. It returns EIO if tx_err is set, ESHUTDOWN if the pool is suspended, and ERESTART (setting tx_wait_dirty) if the tx is not already dirty-delayed and the pool needs a write-log delay or a dirty-data delay; all of these happen before a txg is held, so tx_txg is still 0. Then it takes tx_txg = txg_hold_open(...) and walks the holds: for each hold with a dnode it takes dn_mtx and, if the dnode was assigned to the previous txg (tx_txg - 1), releases the mutex, records the hold in tx_needassign_txh and returns ERESTART with tx_txg already set and the earlier holds' dnode references still taken; otherwise it sets dn_assigned_txg if it is 0 and adds a dn_tx_holds reference; it sums the space-to-write and memory-to-hold counters. It computes the worst-case asize and, if tx_dir is set and asize != 0, calls dsl_dir_tempreserve_space; a non-zero result is returned as is, again with tx_txg set and the dnode holds in place (it does not undo anything here, the caller's dmu_tx_unassign releases the txg hold and the dnode holds, but it does not clear tx_tempreserve_cookie). On success it bumps a statistic and returns 0. The throttle delay checks are skipped when tx_dirty_delayed is already set, so the delay returns are not unconditional.
note: Reviewers: original right (on a tempreserve error it returns non-zero with tx_txg set); round 2 right (the unassign path does not clear the tempreserve cookie, dmu_tx.c:1154-1186); round 15 right (the delays are guarded by !tx_dirty_delayed, 1071, 1078). Callees not read.

name: dmu_tx_assign
prose: Assigns a transaction to a txg (dmu_tx.c:1232-1323). It asserts tx_txg == 0, valid flags (DMU_TX_WAIT, NOTHROTTLE, SUSPEND; SUSPEND requires WAIT), not in syncing context, and that the dsl pool config lock is not held when WAIT is set. NOTHROTTLE sets tx_dirty_delayed; unless SUSPEND is set it sets tx_break_on_suspend. It then loops on dmu_tx_try_assign: for each non-zero result it calls dmu_tx_unassign (which drops the txg hold and the dnode holds but does not clear tx_tempreserve_cookie), maps ESHUTDOWN to ERESTART (SUSPEND, or WAIT without continue failmode...) or EIO (WAIT with the pool failmode CONTINUE) per the flags, and returns the error unless it is ERESTART and WAIT was requested (so the returned errors are those allowed by the ASSERT: EDQUOT, ENOSPC, ERESTART or EIO). For ERESTART with WAIT it clears tx_break_on_suspend if the pool was suspended, calls dmu_tx_wait, restores tx_break_on_suspend (unless SUSPEND) and tries again. On success (try_assign returned 0) it calls txg_rele_to_quiesce(&tx->tx_txgh), which releases the quiesce hold, and returns 0. The txg itself stays held for syncing until the later dmu_tx_commit/abort (txg_rele_to_sync), so on success the transaction is still assigned. There is no explicit monotonic-txg guarantee in this function.
note: Reviewers: round 2 right (dmu_tx_unassign does not clear the tempreserve cookie); round 15 half right: the quiesce hold IS released on success (1320), the later sync hold remains until commit. Callees not read.

name: dmu_zfetch_prepare
prose: Decides prefetching for a read at [blkid, blkid + nblks) (dmu_zfetch.c:470-689, returns a zstream_t pointer or NULL). It returns NULL at once if prefetch is globally disabled or the objset prefetch mode is NONE; for mode METADATA it only sets fetch_data = FALSE (it does not return). It returns NULL if indirect vdevs are not yet loaded, and if !have_lock and blkid == 0. If !have_lock it takes dn_struct_rwlock as reader; if the dnode's maxblkid < 2 it releases that lock (if it took it) and returns NULL. It then takes zf_lock and scans the streams: an exact or one-off match goes to hit; otherwise it looks for a stride/future/past match: stride and future matches go to future, an overlapping earlier stream goes to hit, and a recent 'past' match refreshes the stream's atime and exits via out (return NULL). With no match it creates a new stream when end_blkid < maxblkid (dmu_zfetch_stream_create), drops zf_lock and, WITHOUT returning a stream, falls to the prescient section; there it issues indirect-block prefetches (dbuf_prefetch at level 1 for the computed range), releases dn_struct_rwlock if it took it, counts the issued I/Os and returns zs, which is NULL on this miss path. On hit/future paths it updates the stream's atime, returns NULL via out if no blocks remain or the stream reached the end (removing the stream if end_blkid >= maxblkid), otherwise it grows the prefetch distance (data distance only when fetch_data is true; with fetch_data false pf_nblks is 0 but the indirect prefetch distance still advances), takes a reference on the stream (zs_refs and zs_callers), drops zf_lock, runs the same prescient prefetch and returns the stream (non-NULL) even when fetch_data is false. The dn_struct_rwlock is released on the return paths only when this function took it (have_lock false).
note: Reviewers: original right (NULL is returned after a stream creation and prescient prefetch; the rwlock is released only if !have_lock); round 15 right (a non-NULL stream can be returned when fetch_data is false, dmu_zfetch.c:584-688). Callees not read.
